feed.title: City of Atlanta will mark Microsoft land donation with community event on Sept. 12

The event will also highlight the ongoing partnership and future plans for the property to benefit the long-term vitality of the Grove Park community.

feed.title: S&P Global Ratings: Hyperscaler Credit Quality Gradually Weakening as AI Capex Surges
feed.summary: S&P Global Ratings reports that the credit quality of major U.S. hyperscalers is gradually weakening due to surging AI-driven capital expenditures, projected to exceed $7 trillion by 2030. The report highlights increasingly complex and less transparent financing arrangements, raising concerns about potential instability if an unrated entity fails. While these companies maintain strong credit ratings, their balance sheet capacity to absorb new technology investments is diminishing.

feed.title: Satya Nadella Sold $43 Million of Microsoft Under a Trading Plan. Is the Insider Signal Really Bearish?

While the large transaction warrants scrutiny regarding Microsoft's valuation and AI spending, Nadella's continued substantial ownership suggests confidence in the company's long-term prospects. Investors should focus on Microsoft's AI revenue growth, capital expenditures, and free cash flow conversion as stronger indicators of its performance.

feed.title: Seattle Times, Newsday sue OpenAI, Microsoft, alleging copyright infringement
feed.summary: The Seattle Times and Newsday have filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging copyright infringement. The newspapers claim the tech companies used their journalism without permission to train AI systems like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot, leading to AI products that can reproduce or paraphrase their articles, reducing the need for users to visit their sites or subscribe. This lawsuit mirrors a similar case brought by The New York Times in 2023, adding to a growing number of legal challenges against AI companies for alleged misuse of copyrighted material.

feed.title: Equinix turns the network into the control plane for enterprise AI inference
feed.summary: Equinix is repositioning its network as the control plane for enterprise AI inference, moving beyond its traditional role as an interconnection provider. Through its new offerings, Equinix Fabric One and Equinix Inference Exchange, the company aims to simplify the deployment and management of distributed AI environments, particularly for inference workloads. These services address the growing need for low-latency, geographically optimized AI processing by bringing compute closer to data and users, leveraging partnerships with Nvidia and Together AI.

feed.title: What businesses really need from an AI off switch
feed.summary: Businesses need more than a simple "off switch" for AI features integrated into their enterprise software, as turning off an AI capability doesn't always stop underlying data processing or third-party access. The article highlights the critical need for granular controls over AI features, data access, and third-party interactions, especially given that AI adoption often outpaces a company's ability to manage it. It emphasizes that contractual agreements with vendors can provide a more robust and verifiable means of control over AI usage and data handling than mere software settings.

feed.title: How asynchronous tools transform team collaboration
feed.summary: Asynchronous collaboration tools offer flexibility and efficiency for distributed teams by allowing individuals to contribute on their own schedules. These tools, which include chat apps, collaborative document platforms, and project management software, are seeing widespread adoption and continuous evolution with new features like AI integration. Choosing the right tools involves evaluating needs, aligning with IT stacks, and planning for AI, while also establishing policies and KPIs to support asynchronous work.

feed.title: PPCC 2026: Bringing AI and your business processes together
feed.summary: The Power Platform Community Conference (PPCC) 2026 will focus on integrating AI, particularly Microsoft Copilot, Work IQ, and agents, with business processes to drive measurable value. The conference, held from October 27–29, 2026, aims to equip business experts, developers, and leaders with the knowledge to build AI solutions that enhance organizational operations through connected systems and process expertise. Attendees will learn how to apply these concepts to their own processes, with practical sessions covering architecture, agent design, security, and governance.

feed.title: Dinesh Keswani Joins Goldman Sachs as Partner and Co-Head of The Core Engineering
feed.summary: Dinesh Keswani has joined Goldman Sachs as a Partner and co-head of The Core Engineering, working alongside Gopi Parameswaran. Keswani brings extensive leadership experience from his previous roles at Nomura Group, HSBC, GoDaddy, Microsoft, and Verizon.

feed.title: Enterprise AI transformation relies on the end-to-end platform: Azure was built for this moment
feed.summary: Microsoft Azure highlights its comprehensive end-to-end platform for enterprise AI transformation, emphasizing the integration of models, infrastructure, data, applications, and developer tools. The article discusses how Azure supports a multi-model strategy, enabling organizations to build and deploy AI solutions efficiently, reliably, and securely across various environments. This approach has led to Microsoft being recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Strategic Cloud Platform Services and The Forrester Wave: Public Cloud Platforms, Q3 2026.

feed.title: Bank OZK preferred series A stock hits 52-week low at $15.74

feed.title: Nonprofit We Make Indiana calls for Fair Share Agreement with Microsoft
feed.summary: The nonprofit organization We Make Indiana is urging local leaders to establish a Fair Share Agreement with Microsoft regarding its data center in Granger. The group believes this agreement is essential to ensure Microsoft contributes adequately to the community and invests in the well-being of local residents. This call was made during a press conference held on Thursday, September 3, 2026.

feed.title: Microsoft naming conventions are getting an AI makeover—and they sound very sci-fi
feed.summary: Microsoft is changing its internal reporting structure to reflect the company's shift towards artificial intelligence, replacing three existing segments with two new ones: "Devices and Consumer" and "Agents and Infra." While "Devices and Consumer" is self-explanatory, "Agents and Infra" is a broad term encompassing AI models, cloud infrastructure, and Microsoft 365. This change will also lead to Microsoft disclosing quarterly revenue for its Azure cloud-computing platform for the first time.

feed.title: SCOOP: Microsoft backs Water Cost Accountability Act in win for Energy and Commerce Republicans
feed.summary: Microsoft has publicly endorsed the Water Cost Accountability Act, a bipartisan legislative effort aimed at ensuring data center builders, not taxpayers, are responsible for water infrastructure costs. This move aligns with Microsoft's recent Community-First AI Infrastructure Initiative, where it committed to funding water improvements and reducing water consumption for its data centers. The legislation is currently advancing through the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, with support from Republican lawmakers like Reps. Brett Guthrie and Gary Palmer.

feed.title: Cramer Warns Broadcom’s $30 Billion AI Bet Depends on a Stock You Cannot Buy
feed.summary: Jim Cramer highlighted Broadcom's ambitious $230 billion AI revenue target for FY2028, warning that it is heavily reliant on Anthropic, a private company. This dependence creates a significant risk for Broadcom investors, as direct exposure to Anthropic is currently impossible. Cramer suggests that an Anthropic IPO would be a critical validation event for Broadcom's AI strategy, contrasting its concentrated customer base with NVIDIA's more diversified approach.

feed.title: PepsiCo hands global media to Publicis amid transformation at CPG giant
feed.summary: PepsiCo has shifted its global media duties from Omnicom to Publicis Groupe, a major win for Publicis which will establish a "One PepsiCo" global media operating model. This move comes as PepsiCo transforms its marketing strategy, focusing on integrating media, data, and technology, and follows Publicis's recent successes, including winning Coca-Cola's North American media business. The decision could lead Publicis to withdraw from the pitch for Coca-Cola's global media account, while Omnicom faces a significant loss.

feed.title: KeyBanc reiterates Microsoft stock Overweight on cleaner Azure disclosure
feed.summary: KeyBanc has reiterated an Overweight rating for Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) with a $600 price target following the company's revenue segment restatement. The restatement provides clearer disclosure for Azure and improved visibility into Copilot businesses, though KeyBanc noted no major revelations. This positive outlook aligns with broader Wall Street sentiment, with analysts projecting a 12% upside potential for the company.

feed.title: Microsoft AI’s MAI-Transcribe-2 undercuts OpenAI, Google and ElevenLabs on price and speed
feed.summary: Microsoft AI has released MAI-Transcribe-2, a speech-recognition model that is significantly faster, more accurate, and cheaper than competing offerings from OpenAI, Google, and ElevenLabs. Priced at just 10 cents per hour of audio, this new model cuts the cost by 72% compared to its predecessor and includes advanced features like speaker diarization, word-level timestamps, and code switching. This move is part of Microsoft's strategy to build its own frontier-class AI models, reducing its dependence on OpenAI and improving its profit margins across its product ecosystem.

feed.title: Making sense of cybersecurity's converging categories
feed.summary: The cybersecurity landscape is experiencing significant convergence due to AI adoption, blurring the lines between previously distinct technology categories like vulnerability management and network security. This shift presents challenges for enterprises in evaluating vendors and streamlining their tech stacks. Analysts are observing new collaborations and innovations, with identity security and data protection platforms integrating functionalities, pushing companies to adapt to evolving threats and solutions.

feed.title: Why Microsoft Investors Should Fear Amazon More Than Google
feed.summary: Microsoft's recent decision to disclose standalone Azure revenue reveals that Amazon's AWS is a much larger competitor than Google Cloud, shifting the investment focus for MSFT shareholders. Despite Google Cloud's high growth rate, Amazon holds a stronger position due to existing enterprise contracts and its new role as an alternative for OpenAI's AI workloads. Microsoft's core advantage lies in its enterprise distribution, but Amazon's AWS growth and ability to attract major AI partnerships pose a significant long-term challenge.

feed.title: JFrog Moves to Secure Agentic Engineering Workflows - DevOps.com
feed.summary: JFrog has introduced new security capabilities for agentic engineering workflows, including zero-touch remediation that automatically steers developers to secure binary versions. The company also rolled out AI-focused security tools like AI Asset Scanning and Agent Guard, and announced support for Microsoft’s Agent Package Manager to govern AI agents' software component consumption. Additionally, JFrog Traffic Controller will block direct calls to public registries, rerouting through Artifactory with support from Cloudflare, Netskope, and Zscaler.

feed.title: Comscore launches AI ad measurement for ChatGPT campaigns
feed.summary: Comscore Inc. (NASDAQ:SCOR) has introduced new AI ad measurement capabilities for sponsored advertisements on AI chat platforms like ChatGPT. Their AI Intelligence service tracks paid placements, measures website traffic impact, and analyzes consumer engagement, showing a significant increase in sponsored hotel-related ads within ChatGPT prompts from March to May 2026. This service aims to provide trusted, independent measurement for brands and publishers navigating the evolving AI media landscape.

feed.title: AMD is Quietly Eating Intel’s Lunch
feed.summary: AMD and Intel both reported strong data center growth, but AMD's fabless model and significant AI accelerator deals with companies like Anthropic and Microsoft are giving it a competitive edge. While Intel struggles with foundry losses and a lower gross margin, AMD is gaining x86 server share and is seen as a cleaner investment story despite Intel's recent stock surge driven by a turnaround narrative.

feed.title: Hugging Face approached Nvidia’s Huang weeks ahead of $12.9B acquisition, CEO tells CNBC
feed.summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, marking its second-largest acquisition. Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue initiated contact with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over the summer, seeking more resources and scale for the company amidst a turning point for open-source AI. This acquisition signifies Nvidia's continued expansion beyond hardware and into the broader AI ecosystem, emphasizing the importance of open models despite recent security concerns.

feed.title: Euromonitor agrees integration with Microsoft 365 Copilot
feed.summary: Euromonitor International has integrated its Passport platform with Microsoft 365 Copilot, allowing users to access market insights and intelligence through a new agent. This integration enables natural language queries within Copilot, supported by Anthropic's model context protocol (MCP). The aim is to provide clients with a faster, secure way to incorporate Euromonitor's data into their daily workflows and decision-making processes.

feed.title: Palo Alto Networks earnings highlight SASE and network security wins

feed.title: Thomson Reuters detects cybersecurity incident, says unauthorized party accessed files

An unauthorized party accessed certain C-Track files in March, which included court records with names and personal information. The company has taken steps to contain the activity, engaged experts, and notified law enforcement, assuring that its products and services remain fully operational.

feed.title: Teradata Brings Enterprise AI Directly to Microsoft OneLake
feed.summary: Teradata announced a new integration that brings its enterprise AI capabilities directly to Microsoft OneLake, the single, unified, logical data lake for Microsoft Fabric. This collaboration allows customers to leverage Teradata's AI/ML engine, ClearScape Analytics, on data stored natively in OneLake, simplifying data architectures and enhancing AI initiatives without data movement. The integration is expected to be available in Q4 2026, offering advanced analytics and AI for diverse data types within the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem.

feed.title: NCSA and Microsoft Join Forces to Drive Zero Trust Strategy, Advancing Cybersecurity Readiness for Thai Organizations in AI Era
feed.summary: The National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA) and Microsoft co-organized a workshop to promote Zero Trust security principles and AI capabilities among Thai organizations. This initiative aims to strengthen cybersecurity readiness across public, private, and critical infrastructure sectors in Thailand, given the increasing complexity of cyber threats and the rapid adoption of AI by threat actors. The workshop provided guidance on implementing Zero Trust strategies, aligning with national cybersecurity laws and global standards, and developing tailored roadmaps for organizations.

feed.title: Microsoft Discloses Exact Azure Sales Figures For The First Time Following Longstanding Investor Demand
feed.summary: Microsoft has announced it will begin providing specific quarterly revenue metrics for its Azure cloud platform, a move long awaited by investors. The company also revealed historical Azure sales, which reached $29.4 billion in the quarter ending June 2026 and over $100 billion for the most recent fiscal year. This increased transparency and a strategic reorganization of its core divisions reflect the growing impact of AI on Microsoft's business model.

feed.title: Microsoft updates segment reporting structure for fiscal 2027
feed.summary: Microsoft announced a new segment reporting structure for fiscal year 2027, reorganizing its business into "Agents and Infra" and "Devices and Consumer" segments. The company maintained its overall first-quarter revenue guidance while providing specific outlooks for each new segment. Azure revenue growth is projected to be 44% to 45% in constant currency for the first quarter.

feed.title: Microsoft to start disclosing Azure quarterly revenue as company consolidates business units
feed.summary: Microsoft announced it will begin disclosing quarterly revenue for its Azure cloud business, providing more transparency about its competition with Amazon Web Services and Google. This change is part of a broader restructuring that consolidates the company's internal operating segments from three to two. CEO Satya Nadella stated that this new reporting structure will define Azure more purely as their consumption-based platform and infrastructure business, emphasizing the impact of AI on the company's products and business models.

feed.title: Intel shuts down Israel AI lab
feed.summary: Intel is closing its agentic and inference optimization research laboratories in Israel, resulting in 13 layoffs. The company cited organizational considerations based on geographical location for the decision, which is part of a broader streamlining and restructuring program under CEO Lip-Bu Tan. This move is unusual for the industry, as other tech giants are aggressively investing in AI research.

feed.title: Is Microsoft Stock Winning The Move To The Cloud Or Just The AI Boom?
feed.summary: Microsoft's growth engine has shifted from cloud migrations to AI consumption, with the company focusing on monetizing AI workloads and Azure AI platform adoption. Successful AI adoption relies on motivated leadership that can merge disjointed process and AI efforts, recognizing that while AI can significantly improve efficiency, it's not a complete replacement for human involvement and jobs will likely evolve rather than be eliminated long-term.

feed.title: The rise of token-theft attacks: No password or MFA needed
feed.summary: Token-theft attacks are on the rise, allowing malicious actors to bypass passwords and multi-factor authentication (MFA) to access systems like Microsoft 365. Attackers achieve this by stealing session tokens or encrypted keys, often through methods like malware, adversary-in-the-middle phishing, malicious browser extensions, live-session abuse, or social engineering. Defending against these attacks requires a multi-layered approach, including implementing zero-trust strategies, user awareness training, auditing browser extensions, and establishing clear identity verification protocols for help desks.

feed.title: Enabling hybrid work feature parity means new enterprise KPIs

feed.title: A look at HTTP's new QUERY method
feed.summary: In June 2026, HTTP introduced the new QUERY method, a general-purpose standard defined in RFC 10008, designed to handle large or complex read operations. This method provides a safe and idempotent alternative to GET and POST for queries, carrying content in the request body without altering server state. It offers greater reliability, observability, and compliance for repeatable queries, addressing limitations of traditional methods like URL size constraints and operational ambiguity.

feed.title: Thousands of Hacked WordPress Sites, One Operation: Unmasking StopAndProtect
feed.summary: Check Point Research has uncovered "StopAndProtect," a large-scale cyber operation that utilizes thousands of compromised WordPress sites to distribute malware, control infected machines, and steal data. The operation combines file encryption with data theft, employing a toolkit of malicious software components including ransomware, data stealers, and a custom chat application for attacker-victim communication. Significant operational security failures by the attackers allowed researchers to access detailed infection logs, screenshots of victims' machines, and the source code of their management tools, revealing the global scale of the campaign with victims predominantly in the US, Russia, and India.

feed.title: A 12 KB Backdoor Hid Its C2 Domain in desktop.ini Whitespace
feed.summary: Researchers discovered a custom 12 KB Windows backdoor on a single corporate workstation that encoded its command-and-control server address in the number of trailing spaces within a fake `desktop.ini` file. This unique configuration method made the C2 domain nearly invisible to standard inspection. The backdoor, compiled in December 2020, used a WMI subscription for persistence and communicated via ICMP and HTTP, but its C2 domain expired in July 2021, rendering it inert long before its discovery.
